title: Independence Day 2026: Redefining Your Financial Freedom Number

faq.a: Your "freedom number" is the total investment corpus you need to accumulate so that the passive income generated from it can cover all your living expenses and financial goals without needing active employment.

faq.q: How does inflation affect my freedom number?
faq.a: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money over time. To maintain the same lifestyle in the future, you will need a larger sum of money, meaning your freedom number must be adjusted upwards to account for future price increases.

faq.q: Should I clear all my debts before aiming for financial freedom?
faq.a: Ideally, yes. Being debt-free significantly reduces your ongoing expenses and the passive income required from your corpus. High-interest debts should be cleared as a priority to avoid them eroding your wealth.

faq.q: How do dependents impact the calculation?
faq.a: Dependents, such as children and elderly parents, introduce additional expenses like education, healthcare, and daily living costs. These must be factored into your annual expense projections, thereby increasing your overall freedom number.

faq.q: Is health insurance enough for healthcare costs in retirement?
faq.a: While essential, health insurance may not cover all medical expenses. It is prudent to also build a separate medical emergency fund to handle co-pays, deductibles, and non-covered treatments, ensuring your main corpus remains untouched.

faq.q: Can my freedom number change after I achieve it?
faq.a: Yes, unforeseen life events, changes in lifestyle, new dependents, or significant shifts in inflation rates can necessitate a recalculation and adjustment of your financial freedom number even after you've reached your initial goal.
